observation_summary: The StrBuilder.contains(char) and StrBuilder.indexOf(char) methods were incorrectly iterating over the entire underlying buffer length instead of the current size of the string builder, leading to false positives when searching for characters that existed in the buffer but were logically removed.
hypothesis: The loop termination condition in both contains(char) and indexOf(char) methods was using the physical buffer length (thisBuf.length) instead of the logical size of the string builder (this.size), causing the methods to scan beyond the valid string content.
prediction: The code will show the loop condition being changed from 'i < thisBuf.length' to 'i < size' in both methods.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff confirms that the loop termination condition was indeed using the incorrect boundary (buffer length) and was corrected to use the logical size, which is a classic algorithmic error in data structure traversal.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an algorithmic error where the iteration strategy for searching the string builder was incorrect. It was scanning the entire allocated buffer rather than the active portion of the string. This is a procedural logic error within the methods, fitting the Algorithm/Method category perfectly.
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'StrBuilder contains usages of thisBuf.length when they should use size'
